newsitem.title: RUSSIA: NATO has covert "anti-Moscow" policy - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: NATO has covert "anti-Moscow" policy - Kremlin.

text.p: The Kremlin accused NATO and its Secretary-General Javier Solana on Wednesday of pursuing a covert anti-Moscow policy and said there was no progress in the row over NATO's planned expansion, Interfax news agency said.

The agency quoted Sergei Yastrzhembsky, President Boris Yeltsin's press secretary, as saying a tour Solana is making of former Soviet republics had "an undeclared, behind-the-scenes" aim -- to prevent any form of integration between those states.

"The West as a whole, and the leadership of NATO in particular, is opposed to any form of integration between the newly independent states -- the republics of the former USSR," Interfax quoted Yastrzhembsky as saying.
"Having called such a line an anti-Moscow one, the press secretary noted that it was perceived by Russia "no doubt without sympathy, but with concern'."

Russia and NATO are locked in an increasingly bitter row over NATO's plans to offer membership to some of the former Warsaw Pact states. Moscow says this would jeopardise its security and weaken Yeltsin's government.
"There are no grounds to say that the positions have started to become closer," Yastrzhembsky said, adding that the "ball is in NATO's court".
